# Septic Arthritis vs Gout.  There were no fractures or joint 
abnormality noted and foot and ankle x-rays.  The right ankle 
joint pain is most likely due Gout because  of mulitiple joint 
involvement (ankle and MTP on Right foot). In addition, patient 
has multiple risk factors for gout attack: CKD, Diuretic use, 
and HTN. She has MSU crystals in the joint. On X-Rays, there 
were no calcifications at articular surface nor space widening 
concerining for pseudogout or osteomyelitis.  Confounding 
factors were >400,000 WBCs in synovial fluid with 97% polys. 
However, fluid cultures were negative and the gram stain was 
negative as well.  Patient was not sexually active and denied 
tick exposure, so gonococcal arthritis and lyme were unlikely. 

She received PO Prednisone, 20mg x3days, ibuprofen 600mg QID and 
Tylenol 2g daily standing as well as ___ PO morphine prn.  
metolazone was initially held.  For suspected septic arthritis, 
she was treated with IV Vancomycin 1g Q24H renally dosed and 
Unasyn IV 3g Q6H. With this treatment, her pain improved 
significantly, her edema decreased, and the erythema resolved.  
Since patient's symptoms improved, her synovial fluid, blood 
cultures and grams stain were negative, antibiotics were 
discontinued on ___. 

Rheumatology was consulted and agreed that her presentation was 
consistent with gout and not with an infection.  She was started 
on Colchicine 0.6mg QD, and ibuprofen was discontinued.  
Prednisone was tapered 10mg x3 days, then 5mg x3 days thereafter 
to be completed on ___.  She remained afebrile and 
normotensive for the remainder of stay.  Patient ambulated w/ 
assisstance of ___ and noted pain at heel and at MTP joints. 
Altough her right ankle ROM improved, she continued to have mild 
pain w/ full plantar and dorsiflexion.  She will require start 
of Allopurinol once her acute exacerbation completely resolves 
with close monitoring for rash, leukopenia or thrombocytopenia, 
diarrhea, and drug fever as well as CBC and Chem 7 and LFTs for 
allopurinol hypersensitivity syndrome (AHS).  Patient will 
require uptightration of colchicine for pain control as needed 
as she is tapered off steroids.  In addition she will require 
podiatry evaluation for fitting of appropriate footware, heel 
pads and R heel spur evaluation.  She has a job requiring long 
standing times. She will require optimization of pain control.
.  
# Episode of Hypotension.  On HD2 patient was noted to have 
hypotensive episode o/n to 80mmHg systolic.  She was entirely 
asymptomatic.  There was no fever, no tachycardia.  ECG was 
normal sinus rhythm.  She responed to 500cc fluid bolus w/ SBP 
incrasing to 95mmHg.  Her norvasc and lasix were held for one 
day.  Her Diovan was reduced to 80mg QD.  BP remained > 100mmHg

___ and Diovan 80mg QD.  Diovan can be uptightrated to home

Her protonix was continued, she was provided with Magic mouth

Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted to ___ with swelling and pain in your right 
ankle and toe.  You were evaluated for an infection, however no 
organisms were found in your blood or the joint fluid.  It was 
determined that you had gout (an inflammatory condition of 
having crystals in your joint).  In addition, you were found to 
have a right heel which was causing you pain. 

Because  you were suspected to have a infection in your joint, 
you were treated with antibiotics temporarily.  For gout you 
were treated with ibuprofen, tylenol, colchicine and prednisone 
(gout).  With this treatment your swelling improved, your 
redness resolved and your pain improved significantly.  You will 
require treatment with prednisone for another three days, then 
start of allopurinol once the acute gout flare is over.

You were also noted to have one episode of low blood pressure 
during this admission.  Because of this, your lasix, metolazone 
and norvasc were temporarily discontinued.  Your lasix was 
restarted.  

The changes to your medications are as follows:
- Decreased Diovan to 80mg daily, can be uptightrated at rehab
- Started cochicine 0.6mg daily, can be uptightrated at rehab
- Started on Tylenol ___ 4 times daily for total duration of 
gout flare
- Morphine 7.5-15mg every 4 hours as needed for pain for 
duration of gout flare.

Should you experience worsening leg/ankle pain, fevers, chills, 
nausea, vomiting, worsening shortness of breath, chest pain, or 
any other symptom concerning to you, please call your 
rehabilitation home physician or go to the emergency room.
